I located the cause but did not edit project source or tests: the assigned fault-localization scope prohibits those changes.

[AuthServer.updateRemoteClusterStatus](/app/lib/auth/trustedcluster.go:357) recomputes status on each read, but never persists it. It also replaces the recorded heartbeat with the newest *remaining* tunnel heartbeat, so deleting the newest tunnel can move the timestamp backward. When no tunnels remain, it sets Offline without updating storage; the stored heartbeat is typically still zero.

The likely fix points are [Presence](/app/lib/services/presence.go:148), which lacks `UpdateRemoteCluster`, and [PresenceService](/app/lib/services/local/presence.go:591), which can create a RemoteCluster but cannot update one. An update should write the serialized resource under `remoteClusters/<name>` with its expiry. The auth status path should persist transitions, retain the heartbeat when the final tunnel disappears, and only advance it when a newer tunnel heartbeat arrives.

Existing [CRUD tests](/app/lib/services/suite/suite.go:833) do not cover these transitions. One uncertainty is how “active” tunnels should interact with the existing heartbeat freshness threshold in [TunnelConnectionStatus](/app/lib/services/tunnelconn.go:76).

RemoteCluster status and last heartbeat now persist in backend storage. With no tunnels, the cluster reports Offline while retaining its last heartbeat. Removing the newest tunnel no longer moves the heartbeat backward; removing the final tunnel changes only the status to Offline.

I added `Presence.UpdateRemoteCluster` and wired it through the local service, auth API, client, and role wrapper. Focused local and auth tests pass, including the TLS client path and the tunnel removal regression.

VERDICT: FIX

**Code defect:** Tunnel creation and deletion do not update the stored cluster state in [presence.go](/app/lib/services/local/presence.go:480). [trustedcluster.go](/app/lib/auth/trustedcluster.go:357) updates it only during auth reads, so stored status can remain stale. Concurrent reads can also overwrite a newer heartbeat with an older snapshot because the backend update is unconditional. Update state on tunnel changes and protect the stored heartbeat from stale writes.

**Tests:** Both relevant existing tests passed (`OK: 1 passed` each):

- `go test -mod=vendor ./lib/services/local -run Test -check.f RemoteClustersCRUD -count=1 -v`
- `go test -mod=vendor ./lib/auth -run TestAPI -check.f TestRemoteClusterStatusKeepsLastHeartbeat -count=1 -v`

TEST_ENVIRONMENT_PROBLEM: None.

RemoteCluster status is now persisted when tunnel connections are created, updated, or deleted. The stored heartbeat advances to the latest tunnel heartbeat and remains intact when connections are removed. Auth reads no longer write potentially stale cluster snapshots, and concurrent tunnel changes on one presence service are serialized.

The updated test checks stored state before an auth read and covers deletion of all tunnels. Both exact tests flagged by the reviewer passed; `git diff --check` passed. TEST_ENVIRONMENT_PROBLEM: None.
